evidence: change-password.dto.ts: ChangePasswordDto.newPassword uses @IsString() @MinLength(6). This is the same constraint as in register.dto.ts, repeated as a literal, which is a minor overlap.
The input DTOs (LoginDto, RegisterDto, ChangePasswordDto, RefreshTokenDto) all combine class-validator and ApiProperty decorators.
The response DTOs (AuthTokensResponseDto, RegisterResponseDto, JwksResponseDto, JwkKeyDto) use only @nestjs/swagger decorators.
The only incoming dependency is authentication.controller.ts, which imports all seven files. The only outgoing dependencies are @nestjs/swagger and class-validator.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All seven files are HTTP request and response DTOs for the authentication controller. They are one concern, the module's API boundary. Each is a plain class that uses the same pattern: class-validator decorators for input and @nestjs/swagger decorators for documentation. There is no logic, no bypass of an abstraction, and no unrelated concern. The only overlap is the password minimum length (MinLength(6)) in RegisterDto.password and ChangePasswordDto.newPassword. Per-endpoint DTO validation commonly repeats a constraint like this, and the two uses are for different inputs, so I treat it as minor and not a violation. LoginDto leaves out the minimum length on purpose, which is correct for credential checking. JwkKeyDto sits in the same file as JwksResponseDto, and it is only a nested part of that response shape.
